title: autotune-runner-and-quant-heuristic-curator
author: Priya N. Rao
release_notes: Adds an Autotune Runner service and a Quant Heuristic Curator to auto-generate tenant-level batching/caching defaults and quantization profile candidates; ships with dry-run CLI for validation and conservative fallback safe-guarding.
description:
Problem: customers with heterogeneous workloads still spend engineering cycles tuning batching, cache, and quantization profiles. We need a conservative, production-safe automation that proposes high-confidence defaults and exposes a dry-run path for ops to validate behavior before rollout.

What this PR adds: Autotune Runner: background service that ingests tenant traffic summaries and candidate sampling traces, runs a lightweight cost/latency simulation, and emits tenant-specific recommendations (batch size, cache window, prefill strategy, preferred quant tier) along with an economy_score that estimates tokens-per-dollar and latency delta. Quant Heuristic Curator: offline component that synthesizes quant profiles (per-model candidate list + fidelity metadata) using a heuristic classifier seeded by prior evals. Both components include: safe fallbacks (conservative profile if confidence < 0.6), rollout annotations (canary -> staged -> global), and telemetry hooks.

Implementation notes: - Introduced pkg/autotune/runner: core scheduling, sampling adapters, and the economy estimator. - Introduced tools/quant_curator: heuristic pipeline that generates JSON profile bundles and an accompanying fidelity CSV. - New DB table: tenant_recommendations (schema added via migration 20260215_01). - Added CLI: bin/autotune-dryrun (runs simulation on historical traces and outputs a diff vs current defaults). - Configuration: feature flag autotune.enabled (default=false) and tenant opt-in via tenant_config.autotune_opt_in. - Safety: recommendations are emitted but not applied; console rollout UI + API required for apply.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1893) - [x] Unit + integration tests for economy estimator - [x] E2E dry-run validated against internal workload sample - [x] Telemetry (metrics + tracing) wired - [x] Migration added

Rollout plan: 1) Enable dry-run in staging and export recommendations for 30 tenants. 2) Validate with SRE and a subset of low-risk tenants. 3) Gradually enable canary auto-apply for a small tenant cohort with rollback hooks. 4) Full apply gated by performance/quality SLOs.

Motivation/context: This is an operational-first automation: it prioritizes conservative suggestions and observability over aggressive autonomous changes. It complements the existing econ toolchain by producing tenant-scoped candidate defaults instead of global templates.

review_comments: Marco Liu (reviewer): The economy estimator looks good overall; can you add a short note in the code about the assumptions for inter-request latency distribution?
Priya Rao (author): Added comments in economy.go and expanded the integration test to include a heavy-tailed latency sample.

merge_commit_message:
squash! introduce autotune runner and quant heuristic curator: add tenant recommendations, economy estimator, curator, dry-run CLI, telemetry

See ENG-1893, SUP-4421
notes_on_telemetry: New metrics: autotune.recommendations_emitted, autotune.economy_score.histogram, autotune.dryrun.diff_count; tracing: autotune.runner.tasks spans with tenant_id tag. All metrics are emitted to the econ namespace and wired to dashboards created in docs/ops/autotune-runner.md.
post_merge_tasks: Feature-flag rollout ticket created (ENG-2031); add tenant onboarding docs and a Console toggle; monitor autotune.economy_score in the first 72 hours after canary apply.
smoke_test_summary: Dry-run executed against 50 recorded tenant traces. Median economy_score delta vs current defaults: -3.2% cost, median latency change: +8ms. No regressions in output quality on held-out evals.
notes: This PR intentionally emits recommendations only — an apply pipeline will be a follow-up after we validate the dry-run results and the console controls. The quant curator outputs are versioned; curator also writes a small fidelity CSV for offline inspection.
private_flags: autotune.enabled=false by default; tenant opt-in required via tenant_config.autotune_opt_in=true
